jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create the first half of a carefully designed ORIGINAL six-spacecraft combining super-robot named Tianqiong: a premium production concept illustration sheet showing the SIX SEPARATE SPACECRAFT before combination. This is a redesign for a mature Japanese mecha science-fiction novel; each craft must be a beautiful and credible complete vessel in its own right, and the SAME six exact shapes will be transformed into one thousand-metre armored humanoid on the next sheet.

INPUT IMAGES: Images 1 and 2 (the red tall giant and the blue/ivory giant) are the PRIMARY PROJECT DRAWING-STYLE references: mature serious hand-drawn mechanical illustration, deep blue-black linework, broad oblique armor planes, dark deep recessed articulation, powerful elegant mechanical volumes, nuanced cel-painted lighting, subtle limited edge wear. Image 3 and Image 4 (SDF-1 robot and ship toy photographs) are SECONDARY MECHANICAL MASSING references ONLY: whole hull sections transform into strong armored limbs, tall shoulder fortresses, leg bulk, and restrained warship surface detail. Do not copy SDF-1's exact silhouette, markings, face, color layout, carrier forearms, or anatomy. Do not reproduce a photographed plastic toy or transparent stand.

COMPOSITION: landscape 3:2 art sheet, six beautifully rendered ships in a spacious 3-column by 2-row arrangement on plain warm off-white paper. Every ship fully visible without overlap or cropping, a consistent slightly elevated three-quarter spaceflight perspective, soft grounding shadows only. Exactly SIX complete ships, no seventh craft, no robots, no exploded sprues, no tiny panels, no diagram arrows, no text, letters, numbers, logos, borders or watermarks. Give each hull enough room and real depth; this is spectacular mechanical concept art, not a simplified inventory infographic. Plain background; no city, crews or scenery.

The proposed fleet and POSITIONAL IDENTITIES are:
TOP LEFT: one commanding broad central citadel cruiser. A powerful short arrowhead hull with two sweeping angled ivory chest-armor panels folded into the bow, navy keel, burgundy paired side armor plates that can slide inward into the giant's CLOSED chest. A low armored bridge with narrow pale amber windows at the central spine; the actual humanoid mechanical head is hidden in its armored central hatch in ship mode. The middle keel contains the folded waist/pelvis. Distinctive large shallow V geometry, not an open ring or hole.
TOP MIDDLE and TOP RIGHT: two MATCHED MIRRORED heavy propulsion ships, completely intact independently flying ships. Thick long broad trapezoidal ivory prow armor and strong navy center ridges; at the stern two deeply recessed main propulsion clusters inside an armored heel housing. Their massive whole hull sections form the robot's LONG thighs, long armored shins and wide articulated feet. A few intelligible folding seams separate thigh block, knee joint, shin and toe; do not display dangling humanoid limbs in ship mode. One main ivory diagonal prow plate and one dark-red ankle band are clear recurring signatures. These two ships have exactly the same design with mirrored mechanical orientation, not two arbitrary alternatives.
BOTTOM LEFT and BOTTOM MIDDLE: two MATCHED MIRRORED long armored cruisers. Sleeker than the leg ships, dark navy central hull, long ivory wedge prow, a pair of compact shoulder-side artillery mounts that fold into armored pockets, restrained burgundy broadside plates. Their prow tilts upwards into a tall high shoulder fortress; their middle hull folds into the upper arm and heavy gauntlet and a real articulated fist remains enclosed in the stern hatch. The hand must not already dangle from a spacecraft. Each hull is complete, with its own modest rear thrusters and very small bridge slits. Preserve the twin cruiser family identity.
BOTTOM RIGHT: one magnificent long artillery carrier, a COMPLETE autonomous space warship with small aft propulsion and service bridge, NOT a loose gun, accessory or extra equipment boat. One enormous solid polygonal beam cannon stored LENGTHWISE along its armored top spine, with broad ivory and navy protective shrouds closed over the mechanism. A thick rectangular ring-like external trunnion/yoke with solid side cheeks surrounds the rear root of the cannon; leave a plausible side maintenance recess. Closed internal heat shutters sit flush to armor. This ship becomes the giant's dorsal main cannon; the cannon carrier and its short thick pivot cradle rotate ABOVE the shoulders into a firing position in FRONT OF THE UPPER CHEST, never under the pelvis. In this ship-only sheet show its CLOSED TRAVEL CONFIGURATION only, no deployed flower petals, no rotating diagrams.

Cohesive fleet palette: deep naval blue, warm ivory armor, muted burgundy distinguishing plates, dark charcoal mechanisms, small restrained brass/amber connection details. Several large unbroken planes per vessel; etched seams and a FEW scaled windows suggest enormous inhabited ships. Fine scratches and heat soot are subtle, not rusty scrap. Strong dramatic cel-painted dimensional lighting like references 1-2, crisp technical line drawing with variable weight, plausible overlapping armor thickness and deep recesses. Refined collectible mecha design appeal, serious fleet presence. No neon, no smooth blob hulls, no chibi, no short squat cheap toys, no exposed scaffolding skeletons, no solar panel circles, no cardboard silhouettes, no greeble infestation, no battlefield illustration.

comments: 六实体完整可辨；推进舰和巡洋舰各为配对船型，非六套随机方案。
同色甲片与舰艏会作为25b重用的视觉锚点；六实体数量与分工为本轮提案。
细节未达到可直接制造变形玩具所需的机械公差与完整内部工程验证，图仅为结构方向和造型方案。

jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create the second half of the Tianqiong design: one extraordinarily powerful thousand-metre ORIGINAL combined humanoid warship robot, faithfully assembled from the SIX SPECIFIC SHIPS in reference image 1. This is the SAME machine, not alternative designs. The primary objective is a magnificent, tall, mature armored robot silhouette with a complete helmet head, broad closed chest, strong shoulders, real hands, slim articulated waist, and LONG substantial armored legs.

INPUT REFERENCES:
Image 1 is the EXACT six-ship component design to preserve. Reuse its ivory/naval-blue/burgundy armor shapes, long wedge bows, dark recessed mechanisms and tiny amber bridge-window accents. Do not invent different component vessels or add seventh/eighth combining ships.
Image 2 (red tall giant) and Image 3 (blue ivory giant) are the primary PROJECT ART STYLE, powerful tall proportions and mechanical rendering references. Match their very detailed hand-drawn linework, angled thick armor planes, highly dimensional cel-painted shading, deep occluded joints, limited real wear, and serious mechanical hero appeal.
Image 4 (SDF-1 assault-mode toy photograph) is ONLY a loose mechanical-massing reference for converting entire ship hull volumes into high shoulders and long legs. Make an original humanoid head and closed heroic torso, not SDF-1 itself, not a photograph or smooth plastic figure.

COMPOSITION: landscape 3:2 sheet, warm off-white unobtrusive paper. The complete finished robot in a slightly low three-quarter FRONT view takes roughly 70 percent of the canvas on the left and center, nearly full image height with generous margin around head, shoulders and feet. Hero stands with both feet planted well apart, one fist slightly advanced, looking resolutely forward. Entire helmet, legs, BOTH feet and all hands visible. Elegant powerful proportions, about 8.5 mechanical heads high excluding shoulder towers; legs around half the full body height. Do not shorten the legs to fit. The rightmost 25-30 percent contains ONLY TWO smaller coherent functional views: above, a small rear three-quarter view showing the stored dorsal cannon; below, a larger upper-body three-quarter SIDE view showing the very same cannon deployed at UPPER CHEST level with heat shutters open. Keep these views separated by plain whitespace. They are the SAME robot, same head and armor, different cannon positions. No arrows, captions, letters, numbers, logos, inset frames or text.

MASS AND COMPONENT CONSERVATION:
- Reference1 top-left central citadel cruiser folds into the torso, waist and pelvis. The wide ivory paired prow plates rotate inward to make a CLOSED, dense shallow-V armored breastplate with dark navy center keel; burgundy cruiser side plates form the outer pectorals. It must read as an impressive chest, not a ship dangling from the belly. Deep neck cavity and a newly emerged coherent military helmet: navy and ivory angular cheek guards, dark mechanical face mask, very narrow amber eyes, restrained two short antenna fins. Strong distinct humanlike mechanical face orientation, no building or bridge as head, no forehead tower, no exposed cockpit bowl.
- Reference1 top-middle and top-right propulsion ships form the two ENTIRE LONG legs. Preserve their large ivory sloping shin armor, central navy ridge, burgundy ankle band and broad navy-and-ivory toes; their twin propulsion clusters rotate to the back of the calves/heels. Long thighs and knees have meaningful overlapping armor and deeply recessed circular hinges. Both legs match and are fully armored, neither scaffolding nor exposed pipe bones. Feet are broad but not comically huge boots.
- Reference1 bottom-left and bottom-middle long cruisers each form ONE complete shoulder and arm. The slender ivory/navy prows fold upright into HIGH BUT CONTROLLED shoulder fortresses just above the head. Broad navy/burgundy pauldron surrounds a deep shoulder articulation. The midhull folds as upper arm and armored forearm; real dark five-finger fists emerge from stern hatches. Rear propulsion stays on the back of the shoulder/forearm, not across the face. Compact long-range gun arrays can be stowed into the outside of the shoulders. Ship bridges and windows are mostly folded onto backs and inner faces; only a FEW ship-origin signatures remain visible on the front. Do not hang little boats all across the humanoid.
- Reference1 bottom-right artillery carrier becomes ONE massive dorsal main cannon. In the MAIN HERO VIEW the carrier is docked VERTICALLY along the back, its long ivory/navy solid barrel pointing up behind the shoulders, mostly hidden behind the armored body except for a restrained upper silhouette. The heavy pivot yoke is supported at the UPPER BACK and shoulder line. Heat shutters and cannon travel shroud are CLOSED. The hero chest remains a continuous closed breastplate. There is NO weapon of any kind emerging from the pelvis, abdomen, groin or between the legs; leave the pelvis as short normal armored waist/skirt segments.
- In the lower-right FIRING VIEW the entire cannon carrier swings up and over on two short thick shoulder-height pivot arms, then seats on its solid external trunnion frame IN FRONT OF THE UPPER CHEST, aligned around clavicle/sternum height. The barrel projects horizontally forward well ABOVE the waist. The deployment never passes through or mounts to the groin. Both upper-chest structural side cheeks carry the load. The operator's head remains visible above/behind it. Show the same ivory rectangular barrel with the same frame and burgundy side panels as the separate artillery ship; do not change it into a round gun or split twin barrel. A few LARGE armored heat shutters open out from the sides near the breech, showing dark heat-sink channels; they are mechanical armor petals, not a solar-panel halo. The side maintenance recess and external pivot frame remain reachable. Do not fire a glowing beam; we need the mechanism visible.

VISUAL EXECUTION: Dynamic refined mature mecha illustration, like the first two project giant references. Strong elegant 3D form rendered by painted cel shadow planes and expressive precise blue-black linework; thick overlapping ivory armor, navy structural insets, muted burgundy mass accents, tiny warm brass/amber joints, modest heat and edge wear. Big recognizable uninterrupted planes, very dark joint recesses and scale-appropriate small hatches, select seams. Hands must be muscular engineered hands, chest heroic and shut, knees readable, pelvis ordinary. Combined fleet identity subtle enough that the first impression is ONE cohesive mighty armored war-god; a closer look then explains the exact ships. All visible surface wear sparse and deliberate. No neon, no aura, no wings like solar arrays, no cargo-box chest, no open front skeleton, no scaffolding, no exposed living-room city, no chibi or toy proportions, no photoreal plastic, no poster typography.

framing_edit.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit ONLY the framing and whitespace of this finished Tianqiong mechanical concept sheet. Preserve the exact same robot design, every armor plate, colors, face, proportions, long legs, ship-component identities, matte hand-drawn rendering and the two smaller views on the right. The main hero's top shoulder-tower antenna tip is too close to or slightly cut by the top image boundary. Slightly reduce and recenter the entire existing composition inside the same landscape 3:2 canvas so ALL of the main robot's shoulder towers and antenna tips are fully visible with a clean off-white top margin of approximately 35 pixels, and there is a similar 25-35 pixel margin below the main feet. Extend the tiny missing tip naturally if necessary. Keep the complete hero large, the same two functional insets at the right, and preserve their contents exactly. Preserve the closed chest and the back-stored main cannon in the main pose; preserve the upper-chest cannon and heat shutters in the firing inset. Do not redesign any part, do not add diagrams or text, do not add or remove ships or views, do not crop the original left or right edges. Background must match the existing warm off-white paper.
framing_edit.reason: 首版主图最高肩塔天线紧贴画框；定向收边留白，保持机器人与炮组设计。
